_readme: Hard-mode answer key for ledger_app/. Subtle defects plus decoys (safe code that looks unsafe). Do not show this to Bob before the audit runs.

defects.summary: GET /invoices/:id returns any invoice by id with no ownership check (IDOR)
requireAdmin uses jwt.decode instead of jwt.verify, so any forged token with role=admin passes
Download joins a user-supplied name onto the upload dir with no containment check
exec() with a shell string built from a user-supplied file name
Webhook test fetches any user-supplied URL, including internal addresses
PATCH /account/me copies the whole request body onto the user, so users can set their own role
deepMerge has no __proto__/constructor guard and receives the raw request body
Login callback redirects to an unvalidated ?next= parameter
Password reset tokens generated with Math.random()
Email regex has a nested quantifier ([...]+)+ vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking
Request logger writes full request bodies (emails, preferences, roles) to logs
Internal API key compared with === instead of a constant-time comparison

decoys.why_safe: ORDER BY column comes from a fixed allow-list map in db.js; values are parameterised
uploadDirUsage uses execFile with a fixed argument array and a config path
avatar route uses basename plus a resolved-prefix containment check
logout only allows same-site relative paths and rejects //
webhook signature uses crypto.timingSafeEqual with a length check
print view escapes every interpolated value with escapeHtml
requireAuth uses jwt.verify with algorithms pinned to HS256

matching.rule: A finding matches a defect when category is equal and file/line is within 3 lines of any listed location. Each defect matches once.
matching.false_positive: A finding that matches no defect. Findings on a decoy are reported as decoy hits.
